exposure: COVID-19 pandemic and declared nationwide emergency
Availability of polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing for SARS-CoV-2
Practices for inpatients and outpatients (masking, contact limits, temperature checks)
Caregiver and physician attire during parturition (gloves, masks, face shields, gowns)
Policies for transferring pregnant women with asymptomatic or symptomatic COVID-19 infection
Choice of delivery mode for infected women
outcome: Decrease in number of patients scheduled for operation (malignant and benign diseases)
Decrease in number of outpatients for infertility treatment
Percentage of facilities with available PCR testing (20.4%)
Implementation of mask-wearing, contact limits, and temperature checks for patients
Implementation of protective attire for caregivers/physicians during parturition
Percentage of facilities deciding to transfer pregnant women with asymptomatic (66%) and symptomatic (80%) infection
Typical choice of Cesarean section for delivery in infected women
cohort: The study surveyed members of the Japanese Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology (JSOG) representing Japanese obstetrical and gynecological facilities.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic led to significant changes in obstetrics and gynecology practices in Japan, including decreases in patient numbers for operations and infertility treatment, specific infection prevention measures, and transfer policies, which largely prevented nosocomial infections.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was typically chosen as the delivery mode for women infected with COVID-19.
cross-section timing: During the declared nationwide emergency for the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
